reference.source: Scriver's OMMBID / Nelson Textbook of Paediatrics
clinicalPearls: Rare autosomal recessive lysosomal disorder from ASAH1 variants causing acid ceramidase deficiency and ceramide accumulation
Classic triad is painful, swollen joints with contractures; subcutaneous nodules (lipogranulomas) over joints and pressure points; and a hoarse or weak cry from laryngeal involvement
Symptoms typically begin in early infancy and can be mistaken for juvenile idiopathic arthritis
Nodular infiltration of larynx and airway causes progressive hoarseness and respiratory difficulty
Severity ranges from a severe neurovisceral form with neurological regression to milder forms with predominantly joint and nodule disease
Allelic to spinal muscular atrophy with progressive myoclonic epilepsy (SMA-PME), a distinct ASAH1-related phenotype

Diagnosis rests on demonstrating deficient acid ceramidase activity and ASAH1 genetic testing; management is largely supportive, with haematopoietic stem cell transplantation considered in selected non-neurological cases
reference.pathophysiology: Acid ceramidase normally hydrolyses ceramide into sphingosine and free fatty acid within the lysosome. Deficiency of the enzyme leads to lysosomal accumulation of ceramide in many tissues, particularly around joints, subcutaneous tissue, larynx and, in severe forms, the nervous system and viscera. The stored lipid provokes a granulomatous inflammatory response (lipogranulomas) and tissue infiltration that produces the characteristic joint, nodular and laryngeal manifestations, while central nervous system involvement in severe phenotypes drives neurological deterioration.
additionalDifferentials: Juvenile idiopathic arthritis and other inflammatory arthritides
Multicentric reticulohistiocytosis and other histiocytic disorders
Rheumatoid nodulosis or subcutaneous granuloma annulare
Other lysosomal storage disorders with skeletal or visceral involvement
SMA-PME as an allelic ASAH1 phenotype
additionalInvestigations: Acid ceramidase enzyme activity assay in leucocytes or fibroblasts
ASAH1 molecular genetic testing to confirm the diagnosis
Biopsy of a subcutaneous nodule showing lipogranuloma with lipid-laden macrophages
Laryngoscopy and airway assessment for nodular infiltration
Brain MRI and neurodevelopmental evaluation in suspected neurovisceral disease
Storage/biomarker analysis of ceramide where available
redFlags: Progressive hoarseness with stridor or airway compromise
Neurological regression indicating a severe neurovisceral phenotype
Feeding and respiratory difficulty from laryngeal and pulmonary involvement
Rapidly progressive joint contractures with severe pain
reference.prognosis: Severe neurovisceral forms are progressive and often fatal in early childhood, whereas milder forms with predominantly joint and nodular disease may survive longer; outcome depends heavily on the degree of neurological and airway involvement.
pitfalls: Misdiagnosing early joint disease as juvenile idiopathic arthritis and delaying metabolic evaluation
Overlooking hoarseness as a diagnostic clue to laryngeal storage
Not recognising the allelic relationship with SMA-PME
Assuming a uniform prognosis across the clinical spectrum
references: Scriver's OMMBID (Online Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease)
management: Consider allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation, which can improve peripheral joint and nodular disease but does not halt central nervous system involvement
Control joint pain and inflammation with analgesics and anti-inflammatory agents and preserve mobility with physiotherapy for contractures
Monitor and protect the airway given laryngeal lipogranuloma infiltration, with ENT input and airway support as hoarseness or obstruction progresses
Provide nutritional support and manage feeding difficulties
Undertake neurodevelopmental surveillance in neurovisceral forms and offer supportive and palliative care as regression advances
Coordinate multidisciplinary care across metabolic medicine, ENT, respiratory, rheumatology and rehabilitation
Offer genetic counselling and family screening given autosomal recessive ASAH1 inheritance
